lines.text: At the end of 1989, Japan's stock market hit a record. Then it took 34 years to get back there.
lines.say: At the end of nineteen eighty-nine, Japan's stock market hit a record. Then it took thirty-four years to get back there.

lines.text: This is the story of Japan's lost decades: the bubble, the crash, and what it teaches anyone with savings.
lines.say: This is the story of Japan's lost decades: the bubble, the crash, and what it teaches anyone with savings.

lines.text: Chapter 1. The bubble.
lines.say: Chapter one. The bubble.

lines.text: In the 1980s, Japan looked unstoppable. Its companies led the world in cars and electronics.
lines.say: In the nineteen eighties, Japan looked unstoppable. Its companies led the world in cars and electronics.

lines.text: Money was cheap. The Bank of Japan kept interest rates low, and banks lent freely against land and stocks.
lines.say: Money was cheap. The Bank of Japan kept interest rates low, and banks lent freely against land and stocks.

lines.text: Prices of stocks and land soared, and people borrowed more, using those rising prices as collateral.
lines.say: Prices of stocks and land soared, and people borrowed more, using those rising prices as collateral.

lines.text: On the last trading day of 1989, the Nikkei 225 stock index closed at a record 38,916.
lines.say: On the last trading day of nineteen eighty-nine, the Nikkei two twenty-five stock index closed at a record thirty-eight thousand nine hundred sixteen.

lines.text: Chapter 2. The pop.
lines.say: Chapter two. The pop.

lines.text: Then the Bank of Japan raised rates to cool things down. Its discount rate climbed to 6% by August 1990.
lines.say: Then the Bank of Japan raised rates to cool things down. Its discount rate climbed to six percent by August nineteen ninety.

lines.text: The bubble burst. By the end of 1990, the Nikkei had lost almost 40%.
lines.say: The bubble burst. By the end of nineteen ninety, the Nikkei had lost almost forty percent.

lines.text: And it kept falling, for years.
lines.say: And it kept falling, for years.

lines.text: Land prices crashed too, and banks were stuck with loans backed by assets now worth far less.
lines.say: Land prices crashed too, and banks were stuck with loans backed by assets now worth far less.

lines.text: Chapter 3. The lost decades.
lines.say: Chapter three. The lost decades.

lines.text: Instead of cleaning up bad loans fast, many banks kept lending to struggling companies, sometimes called zombie companies.
lines.say: Instead of cleaning up bad loans fast, many banks kept lending to struggling companies, sometimes called zombie companies.

lines.text: Growth stalled. Prices barely rose, and at times fell. That's called deflation.
lines.say: Growth stalled. Prices barely rose, and at times fell. That's called deflation.

lines.text: When people expect lower prices tomorrow, they wait to spend, and the economy slows even more.
lines.say: When people expect lower prices tomorrow, they wait to spend, and the economy slows even more.

lines.text: Rates went to zero, and in 2016 the Bank of Japan pushed its key rate below zero, to minus 0.1%.
lines.say: Rates went to zero, and in twenty sixteen the Bank of Japan pushed its key rate below zero, to minus zero point one percent.

lines.text: After the 2008 financial crisis, the Nikkei hit a low of 7,055 in March 2009, more than 80% below its peak.
lines.say: After the twenty oh eight financial crisis, the Nikkei hit a low of seven thousand fifty-five in March twenty oh nine, more than eighty percent below its peak.

lines.text: Chapter 4. The comeback.
lines.say: Chapter four. The comeback.

lines.text: Then, slowly, things changed. Companies cleaned up, profits grew, and investors came back.
lines.say: Then, slowly, things changed. Companies cleaned up, profits grew, and investors came back.

lines.text: In February 2024, the Nikkei finally closed above its 1989 record. It took 34 years.
lines.say: In February twenty twenty-four, the Nikkei finally closed above its nineteen eighty-nine record. It took thirty-four years.

lines.text: And in March 2024, the Bank of Japan ended negative rates for the first time in eight years.
lines.say: And in March twenty twenty-four, the Bank of Japan ended negative rates for the first time in eight years.

lines.text: Chapter 5. The lessons.
lines.say: Chapter five. The lessons.

lines.text: So what does Japan teach an American with a 401(k)?
lines.say: So what does Japan teach an American with a four oh one K?

lines.text: One: a bubble fueled by borrowing can take decades to recover from.
lines.say: One: a bubble fueled by borrowing can take decades to recover from.

lines.text: Two: putting everything in one country's market is a risk. Someone who bought Japan at the top waited 34 years.
lines.say: Two. Putting everything in one country's market is a risk. Someone who bought Japan at the top waited thirty-four years.

lines.text: Three: people who kept buying slowly over those years did far better than one big buy at the peak.
lines.say: Three: people who kept buying slowly over those years did far better than one big buy at the peak.

lines.text: Four: heavy debt turns a price drop into a crisis. That's true for countries, banks, and households.
lines.say: Four: heavy debt turns a price drop into a crisis. That's true for countries, banks, and households.

lines.text: Nobody knows what markets do next. But history shows why patience and spreading your bets matter.
lines.say: Nobody knows what markets do next. But history shows why patience and spreading your bets matter.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Japan's Lost Decades: The Crash That Took 34 Years to Recover
post.yt_desc:
At the end of 1989 Japan's Nikkei 225 closed at a record 38,916. Then the bubble burst, and it took 34 years to get back. We tell the story with country characters: the easy-money bubble, the rate hikes that popped it, zombie banks and deflation, negative interest rates, the 2009 low, the 2024 comeback, and the lessons for anyone investing today.
